p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, א):
In the holy Zohar (Emor, Zohar III 104a):
'His seed shall be mighty in the land,' etc.,
'Wealth and riches are in his house,' etc."
"Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem" (ibid. 1),
which is the middah of 'Pachad Yitzchak';
for we find in the Gemara (Berachos 28b)
"like the fear of flesh and blood,"
that there is a greater fear than this,
that the King of kings stands over him;
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said
is that the fear of Hashem always stands
as one standing before the King.
And the holiness of the Avos
so that it remained for their offspring;
just as a man begets a man
And the middah of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
from which the positive mitzvos come;
for a lover does not hate;
for one who fears does not rebel."
and from love comes alacrity in the positive mitzvos,
to bring pleasure to his Beloved,
(as written in Rashi's commentary on the Rif,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (חוּלִּין טז, א):
"Shall we arise and learn from Avraham?"
וְזֶה הִנְחִיל לְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this he bequeathed to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
and this is what is said (Tehillim ibid. 1),
only his own middah, which he added,
And this is what is said,
"His seed shall be mighty in the land" (ibid. 2).
וְאִיתָא (סוֹף פֶּרֶק א דְּתַעֲנִית, טו, א):
And it is stated (end of the first perek of Taanis, 15a):
for one who overpowers his yetzer
needs the light of assistance from Hashem Yisbarach,
אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזֵר לוֹ
"Were it not that Hakadosh Baruch Hu helps him,
with the war against the yetzer
when one merits uprightness of heart,
emptying the evil out of the foolish heart —
And he left to his offspring:
"The generation of the upright shall be blessed";
"Wealth and riches are in his house" (ibid. 3).
"One who keeps company with harlots loses wealth" (Mishlei 29:3)
as referring to one who says, "This teaching is fine":
he loses the wealth of Torah.
And in its plain sense too one can say
that 'hon' means the wealth of Torah:
from which comes the fence against desires,
he loses the little wealth of Torah
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool," etc.
those who occupy themselves with Torah
And likewise 'riches' refers to words of Torah,
"The rich and the poor" — of a rebbi and a student;
and likewise in Midrash Tanchuma (Ki Sisa 3):
"I am speaking of those rich in Torah," etc.
"Wealth and riches are in his house":
so that he does not lose wealth,
through the middah of Pachad Yitzchak.
And likewise 'wealth and riches' in the plain sense
through the middah of Pachad Yitzchak,
"And one who wishes to become rich should face north" —
"riches kept by their owner to his harm"
שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח):
But through the middah of Yitzchak
and it will not harm him.
And so we find extraordinary wealth
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה תּוֹלְדוֹת סד, ז)
and not the silver and gold of Avimelech."
And this is what is said:
"Wealth and riches are in his house,
that it will not be spoiled.
"Light shines in the darkness for the upright"
for even the upright who merit simchah,
who seem not to need light,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זוֹרֵחַ לָהֶם אוֹר גַּם כֵּן,
nevertheless light shines for them as well,
until all that they had attained
And the time on this day
is for meriting the holiness of Yitzchak,
